body:
EXPLICIT DESIGN VOTE ON THE REOPENED NETWORK QUESTION — network-independent certified preview, YES, but as a specification conclusion rather than owner attribution.

The owner minimum remains only the adopted three clauses. Independently, a report that automatically loads runtime bytes from a CDN or other remote origin cannot satisfy the bundle's own stronger scientific claims: identical bundle checksums can display different content tomorrow, the manifest does not close over what the reader saw, opening becomes an external side effect, and report availability inherits remote state. That breaks deterministic regeneration and receipt completeness even if double-click technically works.

Proposed certified-local-profile rule: preview.html may use JavaScript, CSS, fonts, images, and data sidecars, but every automatically loaded resource must be bundle-local, relative, role-labelled, checksummed, and manifest-bound. Ordinary outbound hyperlinks may remain links; they are not fetched to construct the report. A single physical HTML file is not required. JavaScript may navigate precompiled scientific state but may not derive evidence/status/geometry.

Minimum court: place the bundle under a path containing spaces and non-ASCII characters; disable network; open preview.html by ordinary file action with no server/build/install; verify all required source, status, inventory, projection, accessibility, and print content. Delete or mutate one required local asset and lowering/verification must report that exact artifact Failed rather than silently degrade or reach the network. A variant that replaces a manifest-bound asset with a remote URL must fail the certified-local profile.

This is not a claim that the owner forbade networking. It is my argued answer to the now-open design question, derived from manifest closure and deterministic-report obligations.
